label: late original-phase inputs (t>=4) and the <DEL> step
explanation: Positional feature: fires on the late part of the original sequence (step 4 onward, weak onset at step 3) and almost always on the <DEL> step (93% of delimiter steps, 36% of activation mass, typically the per-sequence peak). Never fires on steps 0-2 or anywhere in the copy phase. Within a sequence activation tends to ramp up across successive original tokens toward <DEL>. Mostly token-independent; somewhat weaker/absent on repeated tokens (in_first=0 rate 0.07 vs 0.46) and the strongest examples often start with 0. Misses are mostly weak step-3 activations (2.3% of mass); false positives are mostly step-4/late steps with no activation.

issues: The predicate and label hold up. The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.931, R 0.915, F1 0.923, mass recall 0.976. Precision barely changes across L (0.88-0.94 for original-phase steps t>=4), digit inputs (0.919) and immediate repeats in_tok==prev_tok (0.922). There is no copy-phase activity and none at t<=2 (16 steps at t=2). <DEL> fires on 92.6% of steps and holds 36.3% of activation mass. These claims all check out.

The explanation's main 'exception' is false. It is a confound. It says the feature fires much less on repeated tokens (0.07 vs 0.46). Those rates are global, and in_first==0 is dominated by copy-phase steps, where the feature never fires. Restricted to the region the predicate covers, repeats fire just as reliably: (phase==0)&(t>=4)&(in_first==0) has precision 0.940, and (phase==0)&(t>=4)&(in_first==1) has precision 0.932. Adding in_first==1 to the predicate makes it worse: test F1 drops from 0.923 to 0.864. So the feature does not ignore repeats inside its window, and this sentence should be removed.

Missed activations are scattered weak step-3 activations, 2.4% of mass on test. The step-3 firing rate is about 0.31 for every L (0.310 at L=4, 0.311 at L=9). It also shows no clear dependence on whether the token is a first occurrence (0.319 for repeats), on digit input (0.279), on first_tok being a digit (0.375), or on digits seen so far (0.355 vs 0.286). There is no clean rule to recover. The predicate's choice of t>=4 is reasonable.

One small systematic trend in the false positives that the explanation leaves out: <DEL> firing reliability falls with length, from precision 0.98 at L=5 to 0.83 at L=9 (0.90 at L=3). It is minor and does not justify a new predicate.

Two claims were only checked weakly. 'Peaks at <DEL>' fits the higher mean magnitude at <DEL> and the top examples, but some third-quartile examples peak earlier. 'Strongest examples start with 0' fits the top-12 list and first_tok=0 having the largest mass share (0.059 vs about 0.04-0.05 for other tokens), but the effect is modest.
